metadata.title: Startup Frameworks and Scenario Knowledge Base
metadata.scope: Cross-industry founder education and decision support; not a ranking or exhaustive framework taxonomy.
metadata.methodology: Framework definitions use academic/university sources. Real cases use publicly readable university reporting and teaching accounts, bounded by source date. Case facts and methodological analysis have separate references. Framework application and stage mapping are editorial, not claims of company adoption.
metadata.threshold_policy: Proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial suggestions, not actions or thresholds attributed to the companies. Reported historical quantities are explicitly dated and qualified.
metadata.source_policy: Only scholarly papers and official university materials. A-series references support methods; B-series references support real cases. Institutional news, founder recollections and teaching summaries are not independent audits or peer-reviewed effectiveness studies.

stages.validation: Testing demand, buyer and feasibility before a repeatable product
stages.MVP: Minimal usable offer under active testing
stages.early_traction: Initial users or paying customers; repeatability still uncertain
stages.expansion: New geography, segment, channel or business model

frameworks.name: Lean Startup
frameworks.description: An iterative approach to testing business assumptions through Build-Measure-Learn and validated learning.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when demand, solution or growth assumptions remain uncertain.
how_to_use: State one falsifiable hypothesis
Choose the smallest credible MVP or experiment
Define the metric and decision rule before testing
Measure behavior, then persevere, change the hypothesis or stop
frameworks.expected_output: Experiment log connecting assumptions to evidence and decisions.
frameworks.limitations: An MVP must still be safe and credible. Shipping quickly or collecting signups alone does not validate demand.
frameworks.evidence_note: A01 is a peer-reviewed conceptual synthesis of Lean Startup. It supports the learning logic, not a guaranteed success rate or this project’s experiment thresholds.

frameworks.name: Business Model Canvas
frameworks.description: A shared map of customers, value propositions, channels, relationships, revenue, resources, activities, partners and costs. Lean Canvas is a startup-focused variant that emphasizes problems, solutions, key metrics and competitive advantage.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use Business Model Canvas to compare business models and their operating dependencies. Use its Lean Canvas variant to map early startup assumptions and prioritize validation.
how_to_use: Choose Business Model Canvas for the overall operating model or Lean Canvas for early problem, solution and business assumptions; create one canvas per model.
Map the nine blocks of the chosen canvas. In Lean Canvas, include problems, customer segments, unique value proposition, solution, channels, revenue, costs, key metrics and unfair advantage.
Mark untested assumptions and rank them by impact and uncertainty.
Test the assumptions most likely to invalidate the model using customer discovery and Lean Startup experiments; revise the canvas with evidence.
frameworks.expected_output: A versioned one-page business model or startup hypothesis map, with a prioritized validation backlog.
frameworks.limitations: A coherent canvas records hypotheses, not evidence. Choose the variant appropriate to the question; completing both is not required. Lean Canvas alternatives, early adopters and high-level concept are prompts within its nine main boxes. Separate models when customer groups have different economics.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: Value Proposition Canvas
frameworks.description: Connects a specific customer segment’s jobs, pains and gains with an offer’s products, pain relievers and gain creators.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when the offer is vague, feature requests conflict or buyers do not see a reason to switch.
how_to_use: Select one customer segment
Rank jobs, pains and gains using customer evidence
Map the offer to the highest priorities
Test whether customers recognize and act on that value
frameworks.expected_output: Prioritized customer profile and testable value proposition.
frameworks.limitations: Do not fill customer needs from founder intuition alone or assume every feature creates value.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: Customer Discovery and Customer Development
frameworks.description: Tests hypotheses about customers, problems and a repeatable business model through interviews and subsequent validation of a sales process.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use before committing to a product or scaling sales; revisit when the buyer, user or buying process is unclear.
how_to_use: Record customer, problem and purchasing hypotheses
Interview and observe relevant users and buyers about actual behavior
Test willingness to commit time, access or money
Validate a repeatable sales path before scaling
frameworks.expected_output: Evidence-backed segment, problem definition and initial sales process.
frameworks.limitations: Interviews reveal patterns but compliments and nonbinding interest do not establish purchasing demand. Discovery is one phase of Customer Development.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: Design Thinking
frameworks.description: A human-centered approach that iterates through understanding people, defining problems, generating ideas, prototyping and testing.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when workflows are poorly understood or usability and service experience are major adoption barriers.
how_to_use: Observe real tasks and constraints
Frame a specific user problem
Generate alternative approaches
Test inexpensive prototypes with users and revise
frameworks.expected_output: Problem statement, prototype and observed usability findings.
frameworks.limitations: The modes are iterative rather than mandatory sequential gates. A usable prototype does not prove commercial viability.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: Jobs to Be Done (JTBD)
frameworks.description: Explains choices through the progress people seek in particular circumstances, including functional, social and emotional forces.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when demographic segments fail to explain adoption, switching or churn.
how_to_use: Reconstruct a recent purchase or switching event
Identify triggering circumstances and competing alternatives
Describe the desired progress
Test positioning or an offer around that job
frameworks.expected_output: Job statements, switching triggers and meaningful alternatives.
frameworks.limitations: Avoid turning a job into a generic feature wish list; interviews must establish circumstances rather than invite abstract opinions.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: Market Sizing: TAM / SAM / SOM
frameworks.description: TAM estimates total demand in a defined market; SAM restricts it to what the offer can serve; SOM estimates what can realistically be won in a stated period.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use to choose a beachhead, test commercial scope or plan expansion.
how_to_use: Specify geography, buyer, product and revenue unit
Build bottom-up customer counts times annual revenue per customer
Filter for serviceable constraints
Estimate obtainable demand from sales capacity, competition and timing
Compare low, base and high cases
frameworks.expected_output: Assumption-linked market model with a time-bounded obtainable segment.
frameworks.limitations: Market size is not a sales forecast. Avoid arbitrary market-share percentages, double counting and confusing transaction volume with platform revenue. Beachhead TAM is narrower than company-wide TAM.
frameworks.evidence_note: Definition checked against the cited academic or university material. Usage steps, stage mapping and scenario applications are editorial synthesis; no universal effectiveness claim.

frameworks.name: AARRR / Pirate Metrics
frameworks.description: Groups customer behavior into acquisition, activation, retention, revenue and referral to guide growth diagnosis and metric selection.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use once real users generate enough behavioral data to inspect conversion and repeat use.
how_to_use: Define a value-producing activation event
Instrument events with explicit denominators and time windows
Segment funnels and retention by cohort and channel
Test improvements to the current bottleneck
frameworks.expected_output: Cohort dashboard and a prioritized growth experiment.
frameworks.limitations: AARRR is not a mandatory sequence or a fit for every business. A09 questions its usefulness for the thesis’s business-to-government case. Define events and observation windows for the actual buying cycle; small samples may be inconclusive.
frameworks.evidence_note: A09 is an examined university master’s thesis, not a peer-reviewed journal article. Its secondary discussion supports the categories and cohort logic while showing a context-specific limitation.

frameworks.name: Unit Economics: Contribution, CAC, LTV and Payback
frameworks.description: Compares customer acquisition investment with contribution generated over time, accounting for retention and, when valuing future flows, discounting.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use before expanding acquisition spend, changing price or committing to costly delivery.
how_to_use: Define the customer or transaction unit and relevant variable costs
Allocate acquisition spending consistently to newly acquired customers
Measure observed contribution and retention by cohort
Compare expected future contribution with acquisition cost and test sensitivity to retention, delivery cost and timing
frameworks.expected_output: Cohort economics and a constrained growth or pricing decision.
frameworks.limitations: Short cohorts make lifetime value speculative. Keep contribution, gross margin and cash flow distinct; SaaS formulas do not transfer unchanged to hardware or marketplaces.
frameworks.evidence_note: A10 is a Yale teaching case linking contribution margin, retention and acquisition cost to discounted CLV. Cost allocation and contribution-payback decisions are editorial applications, not empirically validated rules.

scenarios.title: NONA Technologies: Choosing a viable initial market
scenarios.context: NONA was commercializing portable desalination developed at MIT.
scenarios.problem: The first two markets the team considered were not viable in the near term, according to co-founder Bruce Crawford.
actual_actions: Completed I-Corps Spark and Fusion customer-discovery programs.
scenarios.reported_outcome: Crawford reported that the first 24 interviews ruled out those markets and helped identify a beachhead.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: The article does not name that beachhead or disclose interview-to-sale conversion.
scenarios.analysis: Technical feasibility and a reachable initial customer segment are separate questions.
possible_solutions: Compare candidate buyers and purchase constraints.
Prioritize a narrow use case with practical deployment access.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Interview users and budget owners in candidate segments; document disconfirming evidence.
scenarios.primary_metric: Purchase-process clarity and feasible pilot commitments
scenarios.decision_rule: Advance only with evidence of need, budget and deployability; do not treat interview count as demand.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: The article does not name that beachhead or disclose interview-to-sale conversion.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Economic and societal benefits; NONA paragraphs and Bruce Crawford interview
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: PillPack: Redesigning medication management
scenarios.context: Patients faced repeated work sorting, scheduling and refilling prescriptions.
scenarios.problem: A better online ordering interface alone would not remove the full workflow burden.
actual_actions: Delivered presorted medication packets with timing instructions and supporting pharmacy services.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT Sloan reported more than one million packets shipped since the February 2014 launch.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Packets are not unique patients; shipment volume does not establish adherence improvement or profitability.
scenarios.analysis: Map the whole customer task rather than one transaction.
possible_solutions: Coordinate refills and packaging around the patient routine.
Make instructions and support easy to use.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Observe medication-management tasks and evaluate service usability with appropriate clinical oversight.
scenarios.primary_metric: Task completion, support burden and service contribution
scenarios.decision_rule: Require safe operation and verified workflow improvement before expanding.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Packets are not unique patients; shipment volume does not establish adherence improvement or profitability.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Opening paragraphs; customer touch points and shipment milestone
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Warby Parker: Making online eyewear easier to evaluate
scenarios.context: Early customers asked to see glasses in person even though the company sold online.
scenarios.problem: Customers needed a way to judge fit and appearance before purchasing.
actual_actions: Hosted visits in the founders’ apartment, offered home try-on and developed physical retail.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The article records the opening of a standalone Soho store in April 2013.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: The source does not isolate the conversion or profit effect of any one channel.
scenarios.analysis: Physical experience can complement an online channel when product evaluation is difficult.
possible_solutions: Test assisted appointments or home trials.
Compare channel costs and returns before adding stores.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Compare purchase completion and returns across a small trial of service formats.
scenarios.primary_metric: Contribution after returns, shipping and channel costs
scenarios.decision_rule: Expand a channel only if customer value and contribution justify its fixed costs.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: The source does not isolate the conversion or profit effect of any one channel.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Opening customer visits; home try-on paragraphs; Eyes on Expansion
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Tulip: Replacing inflexible factory software
scenarios.context: Factory tours exposed software that did not keep pace with changing production processes.
scenarios.problem: Large software implementations were slow to adapt to shop-floor needs.
actual_actions: Built an early prototype for New Balance and iterated closely with customers.
Enabled deployment at a single workstation before broader rollout.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported customers operating in 13 countries by July 2019.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Geographic reach is not evidence that each deployment improved productivity.
scenarios.analysis: A small operational deployment can reveal integration problems before a factory-wide rollout.
possible_solutions: Start with one workstation.
Give local process owners configurable tools.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Pilot one workflow and compare errors and cycle time with its prior baseline.
scenarios.primary_metric: Operator adoption, error rate and deployment effort
scenarios.decision_rule: Scale only after operators can use the system reliably and the measured value exceeds integration cost.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Geographic reach is not evidence that each deployment improved productivity.
scenarios.evidence_locator: A new approach to manufacturing software; An engine for manufacturing
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: FarmWise: Turning robotics into usable farm capacity
scenarios.context: The founders visited farmers to understand labor and weed-control problems.
scenarios.problem: Growers faced labor shortages and less effective herbicides.
actual_actions: Developed robotic weeding and offered it as a service.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported deployment on 30 large farms; the founder described robot production capacity as a growth constraint.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Reported deployment is historical and does not disclose customer-level margins or later company performance.
scenarios.analysis: Scaling requires reliable service capacity, not just additional demand.
possible_solutions: Prioritize crops with similar operational needs.
Match sales commitments to machine availability.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Measure full-season service reliability and economics on a bounded farm cohort.
scenarios.primary_metric: Contribution per serviced acre and machine utilization
scenarios.decision_rule: Add capacity only when utilization and service quality support the investment.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Reported deployment is historical and does not disclose customer-level margins or later company performance.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Finding a road to impact; Weeding out farming challenges
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: OpenSpace: Removing friction from construction-site capture
scenarios.context: Early versions required tripod setup throughout a construction site.
scenarios.problem: A project manager said the capture effort made the product impractical.
actual_actions: Adapted the product to a hard-hat-mounted camera used during ordinary site walks.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The 2020 article reported more than 1.5 billion square feet mapped.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Mapped area is not a controlled measure of time savings or profitability.
scenarios.analysis: A useful output can still fail if producing it adds too much work.
possible_solutions: Integrate capture with an existing routine.
Minimize setup and training.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Observe site walks and compare capture effort and usable coverage with the old process.
scenarios.primary_metric: Capture time and useful coverage per walk
scenarios.decision_rule: Keep the approach only if it fits the routine and produces dependable records.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Mapped area is not a controlled measure of time savings or profitability.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Shining a light on construction sites; tripod feedback and redesign
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Wecyclers: Replacing inconvenient recycling drop-offs
scenarios.context: The initial concept asked Lagos households to bring recyclables to kiosks.
scenarios.problem: Surveys indicated that travel to the kiosk was inconvenient.
actual_actions: Changed to household collection using locally adapted cargo cycles and rewards.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported over 6,500 enrolled households and more than 600 tons collected by March 2015.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Enrollment is not recurring participation; reported scale does not establish financial self-sufficiency.
scenarios.analysis: Reduce participation effort while designing a viable collection route.
possible_solutions: Provide scheduled pickup.
Connect material sales and sponsorship to collection costs.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Pilot a compact route and measure repeat participation, contamination and route costs.
scenarios.primary_metric: Contribution per route and repeat collection participation
scenarios.decision_rule: Expand only when route density and material revenue can support dependable service.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Enrollment is not recurring participation; reported scale does not establish financial self-sufficiency.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Opening operational results; kiosk surveys and cargo vehicle redesign
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Fyto: Moving a biological process into farm operations
scenarios.context: Fyto grows aquatic plants using nutrient-rich farm wastewater.
scenarios.problem: Growing and harvesting the crop economically at scale required new equipment and processes.
actual_actions: Developed automated cultivation and ran farm pilots for feed and fertilizer applications.
scenarios.reported_outcome: As of May 2025, the article reported a fertilizer license while California feed approval was still pending.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Pending approval and planned product sales are not completed commercialization or proof of farm profitability.
scenarios.analysis: Test agronomy, equipment reliability and permission to sell as separate assumptions.
possible_solutions: Validate a permitted initial application.
Pilot operational costs before direct equipment sales.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Run a bounded farm trial with independent measures of input use, output quality and labor.
scenarios.primary_metric: Usable output cost and operational reliability
scenarios.decision_rule: Proceed only within applicable approvals and demonstrated customer economics.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Pending approval and planned product sales are not completed commercialization or proof of farm profitability.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Backyard trials; final section on farm pilots and approvals
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Alchemista: Finding the buyer behind group meals
scenarios.context: Christine Marcus interviewed campus organizers who ordered food for large groups.
scenarios.problem: Organizers struggled with logistics while restaurants lacked access to those buyers.
actual_actions: Built a service connecting restaurants with organizers and coordinating meals.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The article reports 40 recurring customers by her graduation.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: The article does not provide retention cohorts or account contribution.
scenarios.analysis: Identify the person responsible for coordinating the job, not just the people consuming the food.
possible_solutions: Offer an accountable coordinator.
Design a repeat ordering process for organizations.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Interview organizers and test a paid recurring meal service with explicit responsibilities.
scenarios.primary_metric: Repeat orders and contribution after coordination labor
scenarios.decision_rule: Continue only if buyers reorder and staffing costs leave a viable margin.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: The article does not provide retention cohorts or account contribution.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Finding inspiration, then confidence; opening graduation milestone
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Locu: Finding a business need behind a consumer app
scenarios.context: The team first developed Goodplates, an app for rating restaurant dishes.
scenarios.problem: Restaurants had difficulty keeping menus and business information consistent online.
actual_actions: Developed a platform combining automated extraction with human data correction and distribution.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported 40,000 business users and an acquisition by GoDaddy in August 2013.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Business-user counts are not paying-customer counts; acquisition does not establish the causal value of a pivot.
scenarios.analysis: A consumer discovery problem may reveal a different operational buyer.
possible_solutions: Prioritize one costly information-maintenance workflow.
Combine automation with review where accuracy matters.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Test the accuracy and labor cost of updating a small set of business listings.
scenarios.primary_metric: Correct updates, publishing delay and support cost
scenarios.decision_rule: Scale only if data quality and maintenance cost meet buyer requirements.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Business-user counts are not paying-customer counts; acquisition does not establish the causal value of a pivot.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Opening Goodplates story; hybrid data structuring and acquisition paragraphs
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Grove: Learning from early users before a broader launch
scenarios.context: Grove developed an indoor aquaponic growing appliance.
scenarios.problem: The product needed refinement for everyday home use.
actual_actions: Placed systems with 50 early adopters in Boston and used their feedback to refine design and functionality.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported a national launch in November 2015.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Early adopters may not represent mainstream buyers; the article does not establish later retention or business survival.
scenarios.analysis: A launch is a milestone, not proof of repeatable demand.
possible_solutions: Test upkeep effort with less experienced users.
Make maintenance needs explicit before purchase.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Observe a full maintenance cycle with users outside the initial enthusiast group.
scenarios.primary_metric: Sustained use, support time and return rate
scenarios.decision_rule: Broaden distribution only if ordinary buyers can maintain the product and accept its total cost.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Early adopters may not represent mainstream buyers; the article does not establish later retention or business survival.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Company formation and paragraph on 50 early adopters
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: Spyce: Making automation serve a repeat customer need
scenarios.context: The founders wanted filling meals at a lower price.
scenarios.problem: Robotics novelty alone would not make people return for food.
actual_actions: Built a prototype, recruited culinary expertise and opened a Boston restaurant.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The 2018 article describes an operating restaurant with bowls starting at $7.50.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Menu price is not unit profit; the article does not quantify repeat purchases.
scenarios.analysis: The customer buys a meal experience; automation must improve that experience and its economics.
possible_solutions: Measure food quality alongside throughput.
Track repeat visits rather than novelty-driven traffic.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Compare repeat ordering and full meal contribution across service periods.
scenarios.primary_metric: Repeat purchase and contribution per meal
scenarios.decision_rule: Retain automation only where quality, reliability and cost support a repeatable offer.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Menu price is not unit profit; the article does not quantify repeat purchases.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Main article before Press Mentions; prototype, menu and opening
scenarios.source_scope: Case sources support the historical account only. Framework selection, stage classification, analysis, possible solutions, proposed experiments, metrics and decision rules are editorial teaching guidance; they are not attributed to the company or proof of causality.

scenarios.title: SurgiBox: Preserving workflow in a portable medical device
scenarios.context: SurgiBox developed a portable protected surgical environment.
scenarios.problem: The team sought to avoid adding cognitive and workflow burden for surgeons.
actual_actions: Designed a compact system around familiar surgical movements and trained users during deployment.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT described delivery of about 50 units on a March 2023 Ukraine mission.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Donation and deployment are not commercial sales or comparative clinical-effectiveness evidence.
scenarios.analysis: User workflow and training requirements belong in the product design.
possible_solutions: Evaluate setup and training in realistic settings.
Coordinate deployment with qualified clinical partners.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Assess usability and logistics under appropriate clinical and regulatory supervision.
scenarios.primary_metric: Setup reliability, training needs and workflow compatibility
scenarios.decision_rule: Advance only with suitable evidence and authorization for the intended use.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Donation and deployment are not commercial sales or comparative clinical-effectiveness evidence.

scenarios.title: Formlabs: Making professional hardware more accessible

scenarios.context: The founders targeted professional printing at a lower price and with easier operation.
scenarios.problem: Existing high-end equipment could be prohibitively expensive for smaller buyers.
actual_actions: Used modern components and engineering changes to reduce product cost while seeking early investment.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The account contrasts a roughly $3,000 starting product price with machines costing $100,000 or more.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: This is a retrospective founder account; it provides no comparable margin or lifetime-cost study.
scenarios.analysis: Affordability must preserve the performance needed for the target job.

Validate output quality and total ownership cost.

scenarios.primary_metric: Accepted output quality and customer total cost
scenarios.decision_rule: Proceed when performance meets the use case and sustainable pricing remains possible.

scenarios.title: Dropbox: Turning a personal frustration into a reliable service
scenarios.context: Drew Houston developed file-storage software after repeatedly losing flash drives.
scenarios.problem: Existing file-hosting services were described as slow or unreliable.
actual_actions: Built cross-device file access and recruited an early engineering team.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported more than 100 million users in June 2013.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: User count does not reveal active usage, paying conversion or cohort retention.
scenarios.analysis: Growth analysis must distinguish registrations from durable customer value.
possible_solutions: Measure reliability and successful file retrieval.
Analyze active and paying cohorts separately.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Track activation and repeat usage alongside reliability for a defined cohort.
scenarios.primary_metric: Successful synchronization, retained users and paying conversion
scenarios.decision_rule: Do not infer retention or profitability from total registrations.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: User count does not reveal active usage, paying conversion or cohort retention.

scenarios.analysis: An analytical tool may need a transaction workflow to deliver the full customer job.
possible_solutions: Support comparable bids and supplier selection.
Track completed projects rather than listings alone.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Follow a cohort from property assessment through contracting and installation.
scenarios.primary_metric: Project completion, buyer effort and transaction contribution
scenarios.decision_rule: Expand services only where execution and economics are demonstrated.

scenarios.title: Quincy Apparel: Demand without delivery capability
scenarios.context: HBS describes promising demand for Quincy’s apparel.

scenarios.title: Duolingo: Separating signups from recurring learning
scenarios.context: Duolingo combined free lessons with translation of real-world text.
scenarios.problem: The launch-era model needed recurring participation and a sustainable commercial path.
actual_actions: Ran a beta and planned commercial translation services.
scenarios.reported_outcome: CMU reported over 100,000 beta participants and about 30,000 regular users under its stated weekly-use definition.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: These are launch-era reported counts, not a modern retention cohort or evidence of translation revenue.
scenarios.analysis: Define engagement precisely before treating a large signup count as traction.
possible_solutions: Track consistent learner cohorts.
Test buyer demand separately from learner participation.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Measure weekly learning activity and test a paid buyer proposition independently.
scenarios.primary_metric: Cohort activity, learning progress and verified paid demand
scenarios.decision_rule: Avoid inferring monetization from free participation.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: These are launch-era reported counts, not a modern retention cohort or evidence of translation revenue.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Beta-user and regular-user paragraphs; planned translation service

scenarios.problem: The team found fundraising fragmented and time-consuming relative to product and distribution needs.
actual_actions: Created a for-profit arm alongside the nonprofit, with differentiated roles and licensing arrangements.
scenarios.reported_outcome: The vignette reports Series A financing in early 2012 and continuing coordination and donor-communication challenges.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: The account does not establish long-term sustainability or make the structure a universal recommendation.
scenarios.analysis: Organizational design should fit capital needs, stakeholder relationships and mission.
possible_solutions: Compare one-entity and hybrid operating models.
Make funding roles and responsibilities explicit.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Review resource flows and stakeholder expectations with qualified governance advisers.
scenarios.primary_metric: Capital availability, coordination burden and mission alignment
scenarios.decision_rule: Choose a structure only after evaluating its operating and governance implications.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: The account does not establish long-term sustainability or make the structure a universal recommendation.

scenarios.title: EduFi: Making education finance accessible to families
scenarios.context: Families in Pakistan faced barriers to financing college.
scenarios.problem: Traditional borrowing could require collateral and take too long for tuition deadlines.
actual_actions: Developed borrower assessment, direct college payment and installment repayment; obtained a license in February 2024.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported more than $500,000 disbursed during the first six months.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Disbursement is not profitability or long-run credit quality; no current lending terms are asserted.
scenarios.analysis: Separate student needs, parent borrowing and the institution receiving payment.
possible_solutions: Map the complete payer workflow.
Validate servicing capacity and portfolio economics before expansion.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Assess completion times and fully seasoned repayment cohorts under applicable requirements.
scenarios.primary_metric: Application completion, servicing cost and cohort losses
scenarios.decision_rule: Do not infer mature credit performance from an early lending cohort.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Disbursement is not profitability or long-run credit quality; no current lending terms are asserted.
scenarios.evidence_locator: Opening disbursement milestone; borrower workflow and February 2024 license

scenarios.title: r2c / Semgrep: Fitting security tooling into development work
scenarios.context: Security review could delay software deployment and require specialist expertise.
scenarios.problem: The founders wanted code checking to fit existing development workflows.
actual_actions: Revived an open-source project during a 2019 hackathon and expanded language support and integrations.
scenarios.reported_outcome: MIT reported use by organizations including Slack, Dropbox and Snowflake.
scenarios.outcome_limitations: Named adoption does not quantify security improvements, retention or revenue.
scenarios.analysis: Developer adoption depends on useful feedback without excessive interruption.
possible_solutions: Integrate checks into existing review workflows.
Let teams tune rules and manage false positives.
scenarios.proposed_experiment: Pilot checks on a representative codebase and compare actionable findings with interruption costs.
scenarios.primary_metric: Actionable findings, false positives and repeat use
scenarios.decision_rule: Expand only if teams sustain use and can act on the findings.
scenarios.risks_and_constraints: Editorial considerations: Named adoption does not quantify security improvements, retention or revenue.
scenarios.evidence_locator: 2019 internal hackathon; workflow integration; customer examples

rag_chunks.title: Lean Startup
rag_chunks.text:
# Lean Startup

Evidence type: framework summary with editorial application guidance.

An iterative approach to testing business assumptions through Build-Measure-Learn and validated learning.

When: Use when demand, solution or growth assumptions remain uncertain.

Steps: State one falsifiable hypothesis; Choose the smallest credible MVP or experiment; Define the metric and decision rule before testing; Measure behavior, then persevere, change the hypothesis or stop.

Limitations: An MVP must still be safe and credible. Shipping quickly or collecting signups alone does not validate demand.

Sources: [A01: The Lean Startup Framework: Closing the Academic–Practitioner Divide](https://doi.org/10.1177/1042258719899415)

rag_chunks.title: Customer Discovery and Customer Development
rag_chunks.text:
# Customer Discovery and Customer Development

Evidence type: framework summary with editorial application guidance.

Tests hypotheses about customers, problems and a repeatable business model through interviews and subsequent validation of a sales process.

When: Use before committing to a product or scaling sales; revisit when the buyer, user or buying process is unclear.

Steps: Record customer, problem and purchasing hypotheses; Interview and observe relevant users and buyers about actual behavior; Test willingness to commit time, access or money; Validate a repeatable sales path before scaling.

Limitations: Interviews reveal patterns but compliments and nonbinding interest do not establish purchasing demand. Discovery is one phase of Customer Development.

Sources: [A04: The VentureLab Process](https://venturelab.gatech.edu/process); [A16: Venture Lab | Customer Discovery](https://ventures.yale.edu/venture-lab/customer-discovery)

rag_chunks.title: Market Sizing: TAM / SAM / SOM
rag_chunks.text:
# Market Sizing: TAM / SAM / SOM

Evidence type: framework summary with editorial application guidance.

TAM estimates total demand in a defined market; SAM restricts it to what the offer can serve; SOM estimates what can realistically be won in a stated period.

When: Use to choose a beachhead, test commercial scope or plan expansion.

Steps: Specify geography, buyer, product and revenue unit; Build bottom-up customer counts times annual revenue per customer; Filter for serviceable constraints; Estimate obtainable demand from sales capacity, competition and timing; Compare low, base and high cases.

Limitations: Market size is not a sales forecast. Avoid arbitrary market-share percentages, double counting and confusing transaction volume with platform revenue. Beachhead TAM is narrower than company-wide TAM.

Sources: [A07: Applying to the Innovation Pathway Step 3: Opportunity Sizing](https://www.bu.edu/innovate/programs-competitions/innovation-pathway/details/applying-to-the-innovation-pathway-step-3-opportunity-sizing/); [A08: Market Research Guide](https://technologylicensing.utah.edu/index.php?catid=2%3Ageneral&id=306%3Amarket-research&option=com_content&view=article)

rag_chunks.title: NONA Technologies: Choosing a viable initial market
rag_chunks.text:
# NONA Technologies: Choosing a viable initial market

Evidence type: documented real case with separately labeled editorial analysis. Evidence as of 2024-10-02; later results are not asserted.

## Documented account

NONA was commercializing portable desalination developed at MIT. The first two markets the team considered were not viable in the near term, according to co-founder Bruce Crawford.

Actual actions: Completed I-Corps Spark and Fusion customer-discovery programs..

Reported outcome: Crawford reported that the first 24 interviews ruled out those markets and helped identify a beachhead.

Evidence limits: The article does not name that beachhead or disclose interview-to-sale conversion.

Case sources: [B01: Translating MIT research into real-world results](https://news.mit.edu/2024/translating-mit-research-real-world-results-1002)

Source location: Economic and societal benefits; NONA paragraphs and Bruce Crawford interview

## Editorial guidance, not company actions

Technical feasibility and a reachable initial customer segment are separate questions.

Proposed experiment: Interview users and budget owners in candidate segments; document disconfirming evidence.

Suggested metric: Purchase-process clarity and feasible pilot commitments

Suggested decision rule: Advance only with evidence of need, budget and deployability; do not treat interview count as demand.

Framework mapping is editorial; no claim that the company used each named framework. Method sources: [A04: The VentureLab Process](https://venturelab.gatech.edu/process); [A07: Applying to the Innovation Pathway Step 3: Opportunity Sizing](https://www.bu.edu/innovate/programs-competitions/innovation-pathway/details/applying-to-the-innovation-pathway-step-3-opportunity-sizing/); [A08: Market Research Guide](https://technologylicensing.utah.edu/index.php?catid=2%3Ageneral&id=306%3Amarket-research&option=com_content&view=article); [A16: Venture Lab | Customer Discovery](https://ventures.yale.edu/venture-lab/customer-discovery)

rag_chunks.title: Growth and scaling
rag_chunks.text:
# Growth and scaling

Evidence type: editorial stage and mentorship recommendation, not a prescribed universal sequence.

Objective: Increase volume while preserving service quality and economics.

Challenges: Acquisition costs rise; Founder bottlenecks; Capacity and cash constraints.

Mentors: Scaling operator; Sales leader; People and finance mentors.

Outputs: Channel economics, operating capacity plan and management responsibilities.

Review before progressing: Repeatable channels and sufficient capacity and cash under realistic downside assumptions.

Method references: [A02: Business models in strategic management: 4.1 Business model canvas](https://www.open.edu/openlearn/mod/oucontent/view.php?id=109250&section=4.1); [A09: Inspired by The Lean Startup – Introducing Experimentation to Improve the New Product Development Process of an IT Service Company in the Social and Healthcare Sector](https://aaltodoc.aalto.fi/bitstream/handle/123456789/37140/master_Linkola_Emmi_2019.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1); [A10: On the Nature of Revenue: Not All Revenue Is Created Equally](https://som.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2025-04/On%20the%20Nature%20of%20Revenue.pdf); [A11: Startup Tools & Templates](https://www.csus.edu/center/carlsen/hornetcombs/startup-tools-templates.html)
